title: Rabbi Chanin (Palestinian)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Berakhot 32b: “Rabbi Chanin said that Rabbi Chanina said”; Dikdukei Soferim reads “Rabbi Chanin said — and some say Rabbi Chanina.” So it is in Eruvin 64b: “Rav (Hyman proposes Rabbi) Chanin said — and some say Rabbi Chanina.” In Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 8:8: Rabbi Chanin in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

In Sukkah 5b: “Rabbi Chanin said: The whole verse was stated for measurements.” In Berakhot 41a: Rabbi Chanan, and Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Chanin. Mostly we find his sayings in aggadah, as in Shabbat 32a, where he said “What is the verse?”; there, at 149a, “Do not turn to your own understanding”; and in Megillah 14a he expounded the verse “Ramatayim”: a man who comes from people who stand at the height of the world. He is likewise mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:2: “Rabbi Chanin said: He explained to us on Rabbi Meir’s words: Therefore he shall leave,” etc.; and in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 7:5: “Rabbi Chaninan (Hyman proposes Chanin) said: He explained to us: there are four kinds of stones.” In Menachot 103b Rabbi Bivi answered Rabbi Zerika: “For Rabbi Chanin said: ‘And your life shall hang in doubt before you’ — this is one who buys grain from year to year,” etc.

notes.text: The supplied פ״חה ה״ח is rendered chapter8,halakhah8 and identified as Jerusalem Talmud; the stray letter remains disclosed. Hyman’s Chanin/Chanan/Chaninan and Rav/Rabbi corrections are not blanket name normalization.

The inspected Berakhot 32b reads Chanin reporting Chanina, rather than the alternative attribution Hyman reports from Dikdukei Soferim. Chanin, Chanan and Chaninan, Rav and Rabbi, and the Jerusalem Talmud chapter label remain occurrence-specific. The exact Dikdukei Soferim readings were not inspected, and “mostly in aggadah” is not changed to an exclusive claim.
